newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Western Australia leads Australian states in growth.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Western Australia leads Australian states in growth.

text.p: The Western Australian economy grew at a trend annual rate of 8.3 percent in the June quarter, leading other states by far, the Australian Bureau of Statistics reported on Thursday.

Most other mainland states showed real growth rates in gross state produce only about half as fast: New South Wales 3.5 percent, Victoria 3.9 percent, Queensland 5.2 percent and South Australia 4.7 percent.
Tasmania's trend gross state product grew 2.7 percent between the June quarters of 1995 and 1996.
The bureau labels this data as experimental, because the inflation adjustment (deflator) used for measures of income is the one calculated for expenditure data.

The trend data -- the seasonally adjusted series smoothed with a moving average -- showed gross state produce accelerating from recent growth rates in New South Wales (which grew 1.0 percent from the previous quarter) and Queensland (1.7 percent).
Victoria's economy was tending to slow, with trend output growing just 0.4 percent from the previous quarter.
